correctness.rationale: Two colors must split every closed neighborhood 2+2. In rung sums t and differences d, this gives t[i−1]+2t[i]+t[i+1]=0 and d[i−1]+d[i+1]=0. Periodicity eliminates the linear term of the alternating t mode and forces t=0 for odd n; d[i+2]=−d[i] permits a nonzero solution only if 4 divides n. Nonzero t forces identical rung colors alternating across columns; otherwise opposite rung colors admit four named assignments exactly when 4 divides n. A proper three-coloring of an odd cycle repeated on both layers is valid. For n≥3 each based closed walk of length n on pairs of columns uniquely specifies the coloring with a fixed column index, including at n=3, so no additional rotation factor occurs. Rebuilt the 81-state, 342-transition matrix and verified the complete factorization over the integers by Berkowitz rather than the supplied Newton-identity certificate; verified named traces 90, 2430, 56574, 1299474 at n=3,5,7,9, and directly enumerated two-color assignments at n=3–8 and three-color assignments at n=3,5. Replay: python /workspace/branches/replay-prism.py (SymPy). The exact determinant and formal trace/log-derivative identity establish every n, not only the examples. At odd n the permutation of color names acts freely on every valid assignment because all three names occur, yielding division by 6.

value.rationale: This applies an established packing-partition invariant to a natural cubic family, giving the parity boundary for two classes and the full optimum degeneracy, not just a color-number bound. In particular the exact odd counts distinguish all legal optima from the much smaller rigid local subclasses and furnish reproducible benchmarks for every circumference. The determinant is a compact all-length result despite its finite transfer computation; there is no claim of an analogous enumeration for other products.
